name: PPI
seoDesc: PPI: work out horizontal pixels from the diagonal screen size and the diagonal resolution. A free other calculator with the formula, units and a worked…
summary: The PPI calculator turns the diagonal screen size, the diagonal resolution and the total pixels into horizontal pixels. That makes it useful for whatever you happen to be working on. Every field is labelled the way you would say it out loud, so you can usually fill the form from memory and only look up the numbers you genuinely do not know.

sections.title: How does the PPI calculator work?
sections.html:
The PPI calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports horizontal pixels in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the diagonal screen size, the diagonal resolution and the total pixels.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: What do you need to enter?
sections.html:
• A measured quantity, entered by default in inches. The unit chip switches it to any of the 34 supported units.
  • A number, expressed in px.
  • A number, expressed in Mpx.

sections.title: The formula behind the PPI calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Horizontal pixels=the square root of ((diagonal resolution − vertical pixels) × (diagonal resolution + vertical pixels))
PPI=(10000 ÷ 393701) × diagonal resolution ÷ diagonal screen size
Horizontal pixels=1000000 × total pixels ÷ vertical pixels
Screen width=the square root of ((diagonal screen size − screen height) × (diagonal screen size + screen height))
Screen width=(10000 ÷ 393701) × horizontal pixels ÷ PPI
Vertical pixels=(393701 ÷ 10000) × PPI × screen height

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Length, opening in inches
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Area, opening in square centimeters
  • Length, opening in millimeters

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The PPI calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Turning a rough idea into a number you can act on
  • Checking a figure someone else quoted
  • Testing how sensitive an answer is to one input
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the diagonal screen size, the diagonal resolution and the total pixels — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the PPI calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns horizontal pixels, derived from the diagonal screen size, the diagonal resolution and the total pixels. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the PPI calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the diagonal screen size, the diagonal resolution and the total pixels, which is 3 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter diagonal screen size in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Diagonal screen size opens in inches and the chip beside it offers 34 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the PPI calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
